title: Frontend direct INSERT into `campaigns` while RLS blocks direct INSERTs
description: Multiple frontend files call `.from('campaigns').insert(...)` but RLS policy `prevent_direct_insert` on `campaigns` explicitly blocks client INSERTs (WITH CHECK (false)).
why_it_is_wrong: The RLS policy will cause client-side INSERTs to fail at runtime, leading to user-facing errors and broken onboarding flow.
when_it_will_break: Any client attempt to create a campaign via the frontend (anon/auth client key) will receive a permission error when RLS is enforced.
downstream_impact: Onboarding step 'Create Campaign' will fail; users will see failures and campaigns won't be created; analytics and dependent services will miss data.

preferred.description: Replace frontend `.insert('campaigns')` with a secure backend endpoint that calls the `create_campaign` RPC using a service_role key.
preferred.code_snippet:
// backend API endpoint example
const campaign = await createCampaignRPC(supabaseServiceRoleClient, { partnerId, userId, name, description, targetSignups, durationStart, durationEnd });

alternate.description: If direct client INSERT must be used, change RLS policy to allow authenticated inserts with a specific claim — NOT RECOMMENDED.
alternate.sql_snippet:
-- Example: allow inserts only for partner owners (use cautiously)
CREATE POLICY allow_authenticated_insert ON campaigns FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM partners p WHERE p.id = campaigns.partner_id AND p.user_id = auth.uid()));

title: Schema disagreement: `partners` onboarding fields differ across repo SQLs and TS types
description: `sqooli_partner_full_database_details.sql` defines onboarding flags (wallet_setup_completed, onboarding_completed, times, metadata) while `final_database_schema.sql`'s `partners` lacks them; generated TypeScript types (`src/types/database.types.ts`) do not include these fields.
why_it_is_wrong: Inconsistent schema sources produce type drift and runtime mismatches; code expects onboarding fields (see `src/utils/verifyAuthData.ts`), but TS types and some SQL do not align.
when_it_will_break: When code reads/writes onboarding flags (e.g., `completePartnerOnboarding`) against a DB that differs from the TS types, runtime errors or missing fields will occur.
downstream_impact: Onboarding UI, feature gating, and any logic depending on these flags may behave incorrectly or crash.

fix.description: Decide canonical schema (prefer migration files under `supabase/migrations`), update SQL migrations to include onboarding fields if intended, re-run `npx supabase gen types typescript` to regenerate `src/types/database.types.ts`, and update code where necessary.
steps: 2) If `partners` should include onboarding flags, add a migration `ALTER TABLE partners ADD COLUMN wallet_setup_completed boolean DEFAULT false;` etc.
3) Run `npx supabase gen types typescript --schema public > src/types/database.types.ts` and commit.
4) Run full test of onboarding flows in staging.
